placements.why: This envelope's entire content is an observatory instrument calibration record — naming the instrument, the calibration value, and the reference standard it was checked against. No existing strata category holds calibration-as-organizational-subject-matter (existing strata is empty for this repo), and the org's named strata vocabulary explicitly includes 'Calibration' as a top-level category. This is the first content in the repo that calls for it, so it is minted standalone, with no parent required.
placements.title: calibration becomes a standing organizational practice with its own verified record, not a one-off adjustment
placements.frame: does this content establish, maintain, or reference a repeatable organizational practice of verifying instruments against held reference standards, rather than reporting a single isolated adjustment?

placements.title: an instrument's calibration is established through verification against a held reference standard, not through the calibration value alone
placements.frame: does this expression ground its calibration claim in verification against a specific reference standard, and does that verification hold across the instrument's full operating range?
placements.why: src-1 states the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration in narrative prose and grounds it in verification against the June reference plates holding across the full observing band; src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument, value, and reference-plate verification as structured field-label entries. All three carry the same underlying content subject — a calibration claim anchored in checked verification against a held standard — which is a theme future calibration envelopes for other instruments will keep feeding, not a one-time fact standing alone. The existing graph structure is empty for this repo, so no reuse target exists; this leaf is minted under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
